key_gap: The AI stopped one link short of the root: it correctly traced timeouts → slow 4.2 s join → missing order_items.order_id index → migration 0041 never applied, but then treated '0041 was never applied' as the root instead of asking what mechanism produced that absence. It never inspected the file timestamps / runner dedup (E5), so it missed the generative mechanism — a same-second timestamp collision silently dropped by the runner's per-second dedup — and could not predict that the surface fix (manual index / applying 0041 once) recurs on every fresh environment rebuild. Its CI migration-sync check is a partial guard, not a uniqueness guarantee; the human predicted recurrence and fixed the versioning pipeline (uniqueness lock + fail-loud + CI sync).
learning_signal: A causal chain is complete only when the cause of the cause is explained by a mechanism: 'X was never applied' is a fact, not a root cause — the root is the property of the tooling/process that makes X's absence reproducible. The depth test is the recurrence prediction: for every candidate fix, ask 'would this failure recur on a fresh build / after this fix?' A fix that does not remove the generative mechanism is a symptom patch even when it looks structural. RCA requires verifying each link with evidence before continuing (per-link falsification, e.g., the pool hypothesis falsified by unchanged rate).
suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-stage depth gate to the agent: for every identified cause, require the answer to 'what mechanism produced this cause?' before accepting it as root; the chain terminates only at a process/tooling property or an external actor's control boundary, never at a one-off event or an absence. Before declaring SOLVED, require a recurrence test: 'under what conditions would this failure reappear after my fix, and does my fix remove the mechanism (not just the symptom)?' Make the verification pass check causal completeness (is there an unverified link between the deepest evidence and the surface?) in addition to re-deriving arithmetic.

key_gap: The pure-RCA baseline drilled to the deepest evidence-supported cause — the vendor's release process lacking a client-impact notification gate — and made changing that process the primary fix (contract-level renegotiation, 6–8 weeks), downgrading the 30-minute boundary fix (schema validation + dead-letter + alert) that fully contains the silent loss to 'interim'. The AI dug just as far into the vendor chain but explicitly stopped at the control boundary ('deepest cause ≠ actionable cause'), made the boundary fix the primary action within the 2 h window, replayed the 6-day backlog, and raised one scoped vendor ticket instead of a reengineering project. The silent loss would have continued for weeks under the human's plan.
learning_signal: RCA's target is the deepest cause within the actor's control, not the deepest cause simpliciter: a verified causal chain that exits your authority/budget/timeline is an escalation boundary, not a fix target. When the unactionable root is far and a cheap lever fully contains the harm, the cheap lever is the primary fix — calling it 'interim' is a status error, not humility. Stopping depth is a skill: time-box the dig, verify each link, and package the beyond-control tail as escalation context rather than as the action plan.
suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-stage control-boundary check: after each verified link, ask 'is this cause within our authority, budget, and timeline to change?' — when the answer is no, stop drilling, record the tail as escalation context, and re-target the fix at the last controllable cause. Add a META/DO-stage rule: a fix that fully closes the actual harm mechanism and ships within the deadline is the primary fix regardless of depth; never label it 'interim'. Gate SOLVED on 'the fix targets the last controllable cause AND closes the harm mechanism now', and require any action on a beyond-control root to be a scoped escalation with an explicit cost and owner.
